transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rachel Gomez (Zenith Head of Security), Tom Alvarez (Zenith IT Ops), Priya Nair (Zenith Procurement)

Summary (auto): walkthrough of SIG spreadsheet, identify evidence sources, discuss KMS integration and data residency needs, agree on next steps and timelines.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE focused on financials. With me is Liam, our security and infra engineer.
[00:12] Liam: hey, hi all, thanks for making time. We'll run through the SIG items and try to map them to artifacts you can accept.
[00:20] Rachel: Great, thanks. We're on a tight schedule; procurement wants the vendor risk pack by end of month so we can onboard in May.
[00:28] Priya: yeah, procurement deadline is 05/01, so if we can get SOC and encryption details that would speed legal.
[00:35] Tom: Also want to confirm data residency — some of our EU customers data needs to stay in eu-west.
[00:42] Maya: totally, we'll cover that. Quick agenda: SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML and RBAC, logging and retention, encryption/KMS, and then go line-by-line in the SIG where you flagged high priority. Sound ok?
[00:55] Rachel: sounds good. Let's start with SOC2.
[00:58] Liam: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report, covers security and availability controls, and we also maintain ISO 27001. I can share the latest attestations after the call — there are a couple of redactions for customer names but the control narratives are there.
[01:12] Rachel: when you share that, do you include the period of coverage and the auditor name? We need auditor details for our audit team.
[01:18] Maya: yes, we'll include period and auditor. I'll link to the PDF and a short cover note.
[01:22] Priya: And do you have pen test reports? sometimes procurement asks for a summary.
[01:27] Liam: we have a quarter 2025 pen-test summary and remediation notes. We'll provide a redacted executive summary.
[01:33] Tom: great. Next, SSO/SAML — we use Okta. We need SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC hooks into our AD groups.
[01:42] Liam: Redwood supports SAML 2.0; we also have SCIM for provisioning users and groups. For RBAC, you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. There are a couple of fine-grained roles we expose, but we can do custom roles on Dedicated/Private.
[01:58] Rachel: on hosted API, what's your separation of duties for admin roles vs simple user? Also need admin audit trail.
[02:05] Maya: On hosted we have role types: Admin, Dev, Auditor, Read-only. All admin actions are logged and auditors can request export of admin logs. On Dedicated / Private you get more control over roles and integration with your IdP.
[02:18] Rachel: Are logs immutable? retention period?
[02:22] Liam: Audit logs are append-only in the platform; default retention is 12 months for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. We can export logs or push to your SIEM over syslog or S3.
[02:33] Priya: retention beyond 12 months is important for our compliance program in Europe.
[02:36] Liam: for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention to meet your policy; I'll capture requirements and follow-up with a config doc.
[02:44] Tom: about data residency — can you guarantee data for EU regions stays in eu-west?
[02:49] Maya: yes, we have region pinning on both Hosted and Dedicated; for regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated in your VPC or Private deployment if you need absolute guarantees. We'll provide the region mapping and data flow diagram.
[03:02] Rachel: Encryption at rest and in transit: what KMS options do you support? We need CMEK and HSM-backed keys ideally.
[03:10] Liam: we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) via cloud KMS providers; for Private we support HSM integrations (H S M) as well. The platform encrypts data at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. We'll share our KMS integration guide and an example terraform snippet.
[03:24] Tom: If we use CMEK, how are keys rotated and who has key access?
[03:29] Liam: Key control stays with the customer; we only see ciphertext. Rotations are managed by KMS — we document best practices. For Dedicated, we can show how to do key rotation with minimal service disruption.
[03:39] Priya: evidence — in the SIG we flagged several evidence items: encryption config screenshots, KMS policy, network diagram, and SOC2. Can you produce those?
[03:48] Maya: yes — common artifacts we supply: SOC2 attestation, ISO cert, pen test exec summary, architecture diagram, network flow, KMS integration guide, and logs export examples. Some items are redacted.
[03:59] Rachel: ok, for the SIG row about change management and patching — do you maintain a CMDB and can you provide patch windows?
[04:06] Liam: we run standard change management with change tickets and patch cadence documented; we can give you a summary of patch processes and SLAs. We don't expose the full CMDB but we can provide attestations.
[04:18] Tom: under network security, do you allow IP allowlisting, and do you have a private link or VPN option?
[04:24] Liam: yes, we support IP allowlisting for Hosted, and Dedicated/Private supports VPC peering, private link, and customer-managed VPN. We'll attach our network options doc.
[04:36] Priya: one of our legal asks is about subcontractors and third-party processors — can you list major subprocessors?
[04:42] Maya: we have a subprocessors list (CDN, monitoring, cloud provider) and we maintain a public list; we'll include current vendors and contract terms.
[04:50] Rachel: For incident response and breach notification — what's your SLA for notifying customers?
[04:55] Liam: We have an incident response policy; customers get initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed breaches with follow-ups. We can supply our IR playbook overview and contact matrix.
[05:06] Maya: moving to SIG line-by-line — Priya, you marked about 20 high-priority rows. Which ones should we tackle first?
[05:12] Priya: encryption, SSO, audit logs, data residency, and SOC artifacts are top. Also a question about runbooks and backups.
[05:20] Liam: backups are encrypted, daily snapshots, and we can provide retention configuration; for Private you control snapshot destinations.
[05:28] Rachel: for audit logs, can we get a sample log format? we want column mapping to ingest into Splunk.
[05:35] Liam: yes, we'll provide a sample export and mapping doc; we support JSON line format and syslog export.
[05:43] Tom: any limitations for streaming responses and logs? like PII redaction?
[05:48] Maya: we offer redaction tooling and content filtering via prompt controls; we also provide guidelines for excluding sensitive PII from logs.
[05:56] Priya: on the SIG question about encryption key custodianship, we need clear language: do you have access to unencrypted customer data?
[06:03] Liam: no, in CMEK configurations keys are controlled by the customer and we only process ciphertext; for hosted default keys Redwood manages them but we still segregate access and have strong controls. We'll call that out in the artifact.
[06:14] Rachel: for legal, we need contractual language about data processing, subprocessors, and breach notification. Is there a standard DPA we can review?
[06:20] Maya: yes, we'll include the DPA. For enterprise customers we can negotiate specific terms.
[06:25] Priya: what about SSO provisioning SCIM attributes — we use email, role, department, and a couple of custom attributes.
[06:33] Liam: SCIM supports custom attributes; we'll provide attribute mappings and an example provisioning payload.
[06:39] Maya: okay, I want to call out one nuance: for KV cache and inference cache items, PII can be cached if prompts contain them; we have prefix caching controls and opts to disable or TTL short.
[06:51] Rachel: that matters. We can't have long-lived PII in cache. How do you purge caches?
[06:56] Liam: caches are TTL-based and can be invalidated; for Dedicated you can configure shorter TTLs or disable caching on certain routes. We'll provide a cache control guide.
[07:08] Tom: Regarding performance vs encryption overhead — do you see latency impact with CMEK?
[07:13] Liam: small impact on cold start for some flows but generally negligible. For high throughput we recommend Dedicated with pre-warmed lanes.
[07:22] Rachel: any reference benchmarks?
[07:24] Maya: we have benchmarks per model and deployment type; I'll share a short performance sheet showing latency with CMEK and without.
[07:33] Priya: procurement question — pricing for Dedicated if we require Private networking and CMEK?
[07:39] Maya: that's an enterprise discussion but ballpark pricing will be in the quote; we can propose reserved capacity options to meet throughput and compliance needs.
[07:48] Liam: also worth noting our routing policies can keep customer data in-region to meet residency constraints.
[07:54] Rachel: ok, for the SIG evidence list, what's the realistic delivery timeline?
[07:58] Maya: immediate items (SOC2, ISO cert, pen-test summary, DPA) we can share within 48 hours. Network diagrams, KMS integration notes, and sample logs we can provide in 3-5 business days.
[08:11] Priya: that works for procurement. Can we get a single link with all artifacts and a short walk-through doc?
[08:16] Maya: yes, we'll prepare a shared folder and a cover note mapping SIG rows to artifacts.
[08:22] Tom: about encryption algorithm and approved ciphers — do you support AES-GCM?
[08:27] Liam: yes, AES-GCM for at-rest envelope encryption, TLS 1.2+ and we can provide cipher lists.
[08:33] Rachel: any compliance certifications beyond SOC and ISO?
[08:36] Maya: we also have PCI scoping for some customers and a few region-specific assessments; we'll list everything in the artifact pack.
[08:44] Priya: for evidence that mentions change control, can you provide a sample change ticket redacted?
[08:49] Liam: we can provide template redacted tickets and process doc.
[08:54] Maya: let's put some concrete owners — Liam will assemble the KMS/network diagrams and sample logs; I'll upload SOC2/ISO and DPA; Priya/Rachel you'll update the SIG and mark anything critical.
[09:06] Priya: agreed. Also want to plan the KMS deep dive — technical folks only.
[09:11] Liam: yes, we'll schedule a KMS/infra deep dive; we'll bring our infra architect.
[09:16] Rachel: proposed date?
[09:18] Maya: how about next Wed 2026-04-22?
[09:21] Tom: that works for us.
[09:23] Priya: ok.
[09:24] Maya: quick note on evidence handling — some artifacts have customer names redacted; if legal needs full versions we'll do a secure exchange under NDA or via your SFTP.
[09:34] Rachel: we'll follow whatever's easiest; secure link preferred.
[09:37] Liam: we also can generate signed hashes for artifacts on request.
[09:42] Tom: any open security concerns we should flag now?
[09:45] Rachel: nothing blocking; mostly just need timelines and the DPA review.
[09:49] Maya: okay, I'm going to recap next steps now.
[09:52] Maya: action items: I'll upload SOC2, ISO cert, DPA and the pen test summary within 48 hours; Liam will share KMS integration notes, network diagram, and sample logs in ~3 business days; Zenith to fill SIG spreadsheet and return with high-priority items by 2026-04-22; schedule KMS deep dive for 2026-04-22.
[10:12] Priya: thank you.
[10:13] Rachel: thanks folks, appreciate the clarity.
[10:15] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and calendar invite for the deep dive.
[10:20] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, e.g., 'H S M' for HSM, 'K V cache' for KV cache, 'Redwood Dedicate' heard once. There are filler words and short cross-talk segments that reflect natural speech.
